lawyer:
Shahabuddin Ahmad, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner. 
Nikhilesh Dutta, Advocate ----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Muslim (Md) ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Abdul Motaleb and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment: 9. Learned Advocate further submits that the appellate Court committed error of law in holding that the vendor of the plaintiff Jamina Khatun having sold out her portion of the ancestral property on 21-4-1969 to the father of the defendants and that the plaintiffs being subsequent purchaser from Jamina Khatoon their suit was not properly framed and such findings of the appellate court are not based on proper appreciation of the documentary evidences on record and, as such, committed error of law which has occasioned failure of justice. Mr Ahmed further contends that the Judgment of the appellate Court is not a judgment of reversal inasmuch as the trial Court specifically found that the defendant could not produce agreement, receipt or any other documents nor even any oral evidences by any DWs to prove or to substantiate claim of the defendants to the effect that the plaintiff No. 2 was inducted as the monthly tenant under the wife of the defendant No. 1 But the appellate Court did not record any findings whatsoever, reversing the specific findings of the trial Court and in dismissing the suit committed error of law which calls for interference by this Court. He further submits that the trial Court upon considering the evidence of PWs came to the conclusion that Jamina Khatoon is the fufu of the defendants and the plaintiff No.1 purchased the suit land and got possession from their fufu and acquired good title, interest and possession in the suit land. But the appellate Court wrongly held that Jamina Khatoon sold the suit land long before by Exhibit A kabala dated 21-4-1969 though the kabala does not contain the disputed plot No. 70 of mouza Padhua and such assertion was not made in written statement and in spite of the fact that Jamina Khatoon the vendor of the plaintiff herself appeared before the Court and examined as PW 2 and denied the execution of the so-called kabala dated 21-4-1969 and in that view of the matter the finding of the appellate Court appears to be perverse and in coming to such findings and decision committed error of law which calls for interference by this Court. Learned Advocate further submits that the dispossession was proved by PWs 3 and 4 and with regard to dispossession of the plaintiff during the pendency of the suit the DW 1 was cross-examined and having considered the evidence along with the evidences of PWs 3 and 4 and cross-examination of DW 1 the trial Court found that the defendants dispossessed the plaintiffs after filing of the suit and also issuance of ad interim order of temporary injunction and submits that Appellate Court having without reasons reversed the findings of the trial Court and setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court committed error of law which has occasioned failure of justice. He again contends that the defendants themselves admitted the possession of the plaintiffs but such admission was completely ignored by the appellate Court and dismissed the suit for permanent injunction in spite of admitted possession of the plaintiffs and, as such, committed error of law, which has occasioned failure of justice. Lastly, Mr Ahmad submits that the decree passed by the Assistant Judge asking the defendants to restore the possession should not be taken as personal relief but has to be considered right in rem and whenever any report as to violation of order of the court is brought to the notice of court of justice in that case the court of justice should use the legal sword to stop the violation of the order of courts and the wrongdoer should feel that the courts of justice are active to administer justice, whenever such action is necessary on issuance of mandatory order and in the present case the trial Court directing the defendant No. 1 to remove the structure has upheld the supremacy of the court and the appellate Court in passing the impugned judgment contrary to the materials on record committed an error of law which has occasioned failure of justice.
